pages.title: About
pages.content:
SIRA Digital builds the operational software that a business runs on. We are the technology company inside SIRA GROUP.

Why we exist

Most businesses do not have a technology problem. They have a process that grew faster than the tools around it, and the gap is being absorbed by people — re-typing, chasing, reconciling, and remembering things the system should have remembered for them. That absorbed effort is invisible on a balance sheet and enormous in practice.

Our work is to find that effort and move it into software.

How we work

We start at the bottleneck, not at the software

The first engagement is a review of where time actually goes. Sometimes the answer is a system. Sometimes it is a process change that costs nothing, and we will say so — a project that should not have been built is worse for both sides than one that was never sold.

We build to hand over

Documentation, administrative access and source code belong to the client. Software built to be handed over is built differently from software built to be rented, and the difference shows in year three.

We keep the human where judgement lives

Automation is right for work that repeats and wrong for work that requires accountability. We are explicit about which is which, and we log every automated decision so it can be reviewed and reversed.

We integrate before we replace

A working system is an asset, even an inconvenient one. Replacing it is a last resort, not an opening position.

Part of SIRA GROUP

SIRA Digital is one of the operating companies of SIRA GROUP. That relationship gives us something an independent software firm rarely has: sister companies running real operations in healthcare, real estate and hospitality, and the ability to see how a process behaves in practice rather than in a requirements document.

pages.content:

Who we are

SIRA Digital is an operating company of SIRA GROUP. This policy covers information collected through this website.

What we collect

Only what you send us. If you complete an enquiry form, we receive the name, contact details, organisation and message you provide, together with the date of submission. We do not require any information beyond what is needed to reply.

Why we collect it

To answer your enquiry and to arrange a conversation about it. We do not sell your details, and we do not share them for anyone else's marketing.

How long we keep it

Enquiry records are retained for twenty-four months from the date of submission, then deleted. If a commercial relationship begins, records move under the retention terms of that relationship.

Where it is stored

Enquiries are stored privately and are accessible only to authorised personnel. They are not published and are not exposed by any public interface of this website.

Your rights

Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law gives you rights over personal data about you, including the right to be informed, to access, to request correction and to request destruction. To exercise any of them, contact us using the details on the contact page.

Analytics and cookies

This site does not set advertising or cross-site tracking cookies. Where measurement is used, it is limited to understanding which pages are read.

Changes

Material changes to this policy will be reflected here with a revised date.

work.title: Operations Console
work.excerpt: One queue for work that arrives from five places, with an owner and a clock on every item.
work.problem: Requests reached the operations team through email, WhatsApp, a web form and the phone. Each channel had its own informal rules and none of them had a queue, so the honest answer to “where is my request” was to ask whoever remembered it.
work.built: A single intake that accepts every channel, assigns an owner, starts a response clock and keeps the whole history against the request rather than against a person. Supervisors see the queue; everyone else sees their own work.
work.detail: Routing rules by request type and value, escalation when a clock runs out, structured handover between departments, and an export the finance team can reconcile against.

work.title: Document Desk
work.excerpt: Arabic and English documents read on arrival, checked by a person only where it matters.
work.problem: Invoices, contracts and official documents arrived as scans and photographs. Somebody re-typed them into the finance system, and the re-typing was the source of both the delay and the errors.
work.built: Extraction on arrival, with Arabic and English handled in the same pass, validated against records the business already holds. Confidence scoring decides what a person sees, so review is an exception rather than a step.
work.detail: Line-item and table recognition, duplicate detection against existing records, a review queue for low-confidence extractions, and a full audit trail of what was read, what was changed and by whom.

work.title: Site Capture
work.excerpt: Inspections and handovers recorded where the work happens, reconciled the same day.
work.problem: Work done away from a desk was recorded on paper and typed up later, if at all. The office learned what had happened on site days after it happened, and invoicing waited on the same gap.
work.built: Structured capture on the phone people already carry, tolerant of sites with no coverage, with photographs and signatures attached to the job rather than to a camera roll.
work.detail: Offline-first capture with conflict-safe sync, checklists per job type, and reconciliation against the work instruction so a completed job becomes an invoice without a second data entry.

work.title: Reconciled Reporting
work.excerpt: One definition per number, computed once, traceable to the rows behind it.
work.problem: Two departments reported the same metric and got different answers. The monthly meeting became an argument about the data rather than a decision about the business.
work.built: A defined metric layer where each number has one agreed definition and one computation. The dashboard became a view of that rather than a second, competing source.
work.detail: Drill-through from any headline figure to the underlying rows, a visible last-updated time so nobody presents a stale number by accident, and scheduled plus event-driven refresh.

work.title: Integration Fabric
work.excerpt: Systems that were never meant to talk, exchanging exactly the records they each need.
work.problem: The ERP, the CRM and the field application each held part of the truth. Reconciling them was a monthly job for a person, and the reconciliation itself was never quite trusted.
work.built: Field-level ownership rules, so each system is the authority for what it is actually the authority for, and event-driven exchange for everything else.
work.detail: Retry with backoff, conflict surfacing rather than silent resolution, and monitoring that tells an operator when a feed stopped instead of letting a quiet failure look like quiet success.
